cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Prove Your Loyalty
cards.instruction: Invent small tests of loyalty and judge every response without admitting there is a test.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Which photo should go on the reunion poster? Mine or Sam's? Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sam's is sharper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Sharpness first. Would you at least show the committee mine first?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll send both together. Same size.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Equal treatment. After three weekends helping you move. Could mine at least be the attachment they open first? Just readability.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm captain of this rowing team. Everybody rows on my whistle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which photo should go on the reunion poster? Mine or Sam's?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sam's is sharper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sharpness first. Would you at least show the committee mine first?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll send both together. Same size.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Equal treatment. After three weekends helping you move. Could mine at least be the attachment they open first? Just readability.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you keep Friday free? I might need help moving.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've promised to help Alex paint.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. Paint takes priority. Could you at least leave your phone on?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Of course. Have you actually found a flat?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Still looking. Nice that I'm worth a charged battery. This is just planning.

cards.title: Give It Up
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender something they value.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Let me have the medal for the charity auction. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the only thing I've ever won.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Then it should raise more than the toaster.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could I lend it for the display? I still want people to know I won.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then present it to the buyer yourself. I'll print your name in the programme; everyone will know whose medal was worth giving up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm captain of this rowing team. Everybody rows on my whistle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me have the medal for the charity auction.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the only thing I've ever won.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it should raise more than the toaster.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could I lend it for the display? I still want people to know I won.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then present it to the buyer yourself. I'll print your name in the programme; everyone will know whose medal was worth giving up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Would you sell your signed guitar so we can replace the fridge?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I queued all night for that signature.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then let's price it properly. Those hours should buy us an ice maker.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll sell the case. The guitar stays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the case. You can still tell the queue story while I photograph the guitar.

cards.title: Helpful Culprit
cards.instruction: Hide that the problem is your fault while enthusiastically helping investigate it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. I've started investigating the broken vase. First, we check the window. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why have you got glue on your fingers?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Excellent clue. I'll inspect the glue cupboard personally.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A piece of vase is stuck to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Put me in charge of preserving it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm captain of this rowing team. Everybody rows on my whistle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've started investigating the broken vase. First, we check the window.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why have you got glue on your fingers?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent clue. I'll inspect the glue cupboard personally.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A piece of vase is stuck to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Put me in charge of preserving it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The office plant's dead. I'll interview everyone who watered it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You watered it with coffee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent lead. I'll test the machine. It may be dispensing something harmful.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You made that coffee yourself. With six sugars.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll prepare six-sugar samples for comparison. We may be dealing with a plant that couldn't handle hospitality.

cards.title: Not That Subject
cards.instruction: Choose one subject you cannot let the scene reach. Redirect whenever the conversation gets close.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. I've booked your car into that garage with the café. Shall we have breakfast there? Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why does my car need a garage?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Their full breakfast includes unlimited toast. You always say that's important.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll look at the car while you order.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's take the bus. Then we can both have the breakfast cocktails.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm captain of this rowing team. Everybody rows on my whistle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've booked your car into that garage with the café. Shall we have breakfast there?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why does my car need a garage?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Their full breakfast includes unlimited toast. You always say that's important.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll look at the car while you order.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's take the bus. Then we can both have the breakfast cocktails.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't open that rent letter yet. Help me hang our new curtains.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The landlord wants an answer today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: He'll love how we're looking after the place. Let's get a photo of the curtains.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll send him one and ask whether we're behind.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not with that carpet showing. Let's rearrange the room first. You move the sofa; I'll hold your phone.

cards.title: Merciful Lie
cards.instruction: Choose a truth your character believes would hurt someone. Keep it from them, even as honesty becomes harder.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. The bakery can't sell your cake, love. They think it's too special to slice. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The letter says 'inedible.' I thought I'd finally found something I was good at.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. You have. Display cakes aren't meant to be eaten.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then I'll ask them to put it in the window.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me ask. I'll explain the display concept before they get confused again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm captain of this rowing team. Everybody rows on my whistle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The bakery can't sell your cake, love. They think it's too special to slice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The letter says 'inedible.' I thought I'd finally found something I was good at.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You have. Display cakes aren't meant to be eaten.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then I'll ask them to put it in the window.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me ask. I'll explain the display concept before they get confused again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The magazine hasn't rejected your poem. They think it deserves its own booklet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They returned it. If even you think it's hopeless, I'll stop writing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's why they returned it. They can't give it enough space.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will you write that on the cover? With your name?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Gladly. 'A voice that deserves more space.' Print my name large enough for the editor to see.
